summary.text: 小 means “small.” Its present form has a long central stroke between two shorter side strokes. Early marks are interpreted either as abstract signs of smallness or as fine sand grains; their referent remains disputed.

formation.text: 小 has no settled account of what its early marks represent: analyses describe abstract signs of smallness, raindrops or scattered objects, or fine sand grains. The sand-grain account treats 小 as an early graph of 沙 and proposes that this graph was extended to mean ‘small,’ opposite 大; this is one source’s interpretation, not an established semantic history. Neither the depicted referent nor a sound-based borrowing is established. Accounts also describe 小 and 少 as sharing an early graph before they were differentiated; one account says 少’s lower dot became a diagonal stroke. In small-seal script, the central dot became a vertical stroke between two side marks. Shuowen’s analysis of this later form as 八 plus 丨 is a historical interpretation, not evidence of the original construction.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze forms are described as three dots. In small-seal script, the central dot lengthened into a vertical stroke. The curated image is a modern redraw of that script style, not an ancient artifact; the graphic change does not identify what the earlier marks represented.

Shuowen parses the seal form as 八 and 丨, explaining the marks as dividing something. Later analyses treat this as a reinterpretation of an altered form. Accounts also describe 小 and 少 as once sharing a graph before later differentiation, though their detailed graphic and lexical relationship remains unsettled.

uncertainties.text: The earliest marks may indicate smallness abstractly or depict fine sand grains. The sand analysis does not establish the grains’ name or pronunciation, or show that 沙 was written by reusing 小 for a similar-sounding word.

The cited oracle-bone use 小雨 is reported as an early example, but its artifact has no absolute date here. Other old uses include time expressions and status-related terms; their dates and connection with “small” are unresolved.
小 is reported as a sound element in 雀, but the historical sound relation remains disputed. In the supplied Baxter–Sagart reconstructions, 小 *[s]ewʔ and 雀 *[ts]ewk do not show an obvious rhyme match.

senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze uses reported; absolute dates unresolved; also current
senses.text: 小 is used for ‘small’ in present-day Chinese. The character appears with this meaning in oracle-bone and bronze examples, including 小雨; the examples’ absolute dates are unresolved and they do not establish the graph’s hypothetical original referent.
小食 is reported as an expression for an afternoon time. Its relation to the sense “small” is unresolved.
小采 is reported as an expression for dusk. Its chronology and relation to the sense “small” are unresolved.

limitations.text: The available examples do not establish a dated semantic path between early and current uses, or between “small” and the reported time expressions or status-related uses.

relationships.text: 小 is reported as a sound element in 雀, which is also described as contributing the sense “small bird.” This proposed sound role is not explained by the supplied Baxter–Sagart forms: 小 *[s]ewʔ and 雀 *[ts]ewk show no obvious rhyme match, and no sound-change account is established.

Accounts report that 小 and 少 shared an early graph before later graphic differentiation; one account describes 少’s lower mark becoming a diagonal stroke. This is a historical shared-graph association, not a claim of derivation direction, present-day interchangeability, or sound relationship.

items.period: Modern vector redraw of the Shuowen small-seal form; depicts an ancient script style, not a dated artifact

items.caption: This modern redraw shows 小 in Shuowen small-seal style. The central dot has become a vertical stroke between two side marks; this later shape does not settle what the earlier marks represented.
items.alt: Three black strokes: a long central vertical stroke between two shorter, slightly curved side strokes.
